headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, companies are expanding AI and digital initiatives while financial performance varies.
summary: Media firms show strong revenue growth, especially Disney, but face mixed IT spend signals. Gaming operators report divergent results, with Caesars losing money and Bally's gaining momentum. Publishing sees mixed earnings as AI tools are rolled out. Education players are investing heavily in AI and quantum tech, with solid revenue growth.

industries.summary: Revenue is solid, led by Disney's $25,248 m in Q2. Operating margins are healthy across the board. IT spending signals are mixed, with Disney expanding and WBD tightening.

leaders.why: Largest revenue and strong operating margin

laggards.why: No financial data and unclear IT outlook

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Multiple firms are buying AI tools and filing patents to enhance content and park experiences.

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Skydance is restructuring its news platforms for generative AI licensing.

industries.it_note: Disney is expanding spend, WBD is tightening, while others remain unclear.

industries.summary: Caesars posted $2,940 m revenue but widened losses. Bally's grew 20% to $792 m with expanding IT spend. Light & Wonder and Brightstar show stable margins but limited data.

leaders.why: Strong revenue growth and expanding IT spend

laggards.why: Revenue high but net loss widened

themes.title: Cashless and digital betting
themes.detail: Light & Wonder launched RAPIDPLAY cashless payment systems; Bally's added new wagering software.

themes.title: Vendor partnerships
themes.detail: Brightstar secured multi‑year contracts for lottery system upgrades.

industries.it_note: Bally's is expanding tech spend, while other operators have unclear or neutral outlooks.

industries.summary: Pearson delivered $1,779 m revenue with expanding margins. Scholastic missed revenue targets at $216.8 m and posted a large loss. Wolters Kluwer is neutral but expanding AI tools.

laggards.why: Revenue miss and deep operating loss

themes.title: AI for professional services
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer and Pearson are launching AI‑driven tax, legal and tutoring solutions.

industries.it_note: Pearson and Wolters are expanding AI spend; Scholastic's IT direction is unclear.

industries.summary: Pearson leads with $1,779 m revenue and expanding AI tutoring. NYU and SLU receive major AI and quantum funding. ACT provides neutral data.

leaders.why: Strong revenue and AI‑focused product launch

laggards.why: No revenue data and unclear IT direction

themes.title: AI and quantum research partnerships
themes.detail: NYU gains city‑backed funding for a $284 m quantum facility; SLU partners with WWT for AI research.

themes.title: AI‑enhanced learning platforms
themes.detail: Pearson's Career Studios adds AI tutors and success coaches for adult learners.

industries.it_note: All listed education players are increasing AI and advanced technology investments.
